title: Water capacity recovery, servicing agreements and fast-tracked procurement
subtitle: Water financial forecast, groundwater monitoring concerns, data centre water use, and a push to advance two water projects.
overview: Council met in special session on Mannheim Service Area water capacity. Staff reported the area is no longer in a water supply deficit. Of 30 L/s ready to assign, 10 L/s is available now and 20 L/s is expected this fall. Staff said this could support up to 5,400 homes, 10,500 residents and 5,000 jobs. A further 40 L/s is planned for October 1.

Council endorsed a Forward Looking Servicing Agreement Framework {{vote:m3}}. It lets eligible landowners secure future water capacity, and staff will keep negotiating the agreement terms. Council also approved a waiver of competitive procurement and extra-funding limits for listed water capacity projects, with authority delegated to the Chief Administrative Officer {{vote:m4}}. An amendment {{vote:m6}} shortened its life to June 30, 2027 and requires a briefing for the new Council before the 2027 budget.

Council asked staff to report on advancing the Maple Grove and Cambridge 2W projects {{vote:m7}}. It also received updates on water finances and groundwater monitoring. It asked staff to report on data centre water use. The financial scenarios are illustrative only, and rate decisions will come through the 2027 budget.

decisions.detail: Council endorsed the framework, directed staff to keep negotiating agreement terms with eligible landowners, and delegated signing authority to the Commissioner of Water and Wastewater Services {{vote:m3}}.

decisions.item: Time limit on procurement waiver authority
decisions.detail: Council amended the purchasing by-law waiver and CAO delegation to end June 30, 2027 instead of December 31, 2028, and required a full briefing of the new Council before the 2027 budget {{vote:m6}}.

decisions.item: Review of advancing Maple Grove and Cambridge 2W projects
decisions.detail: Council directed staff to report by the end of August 2026 on the feasibility, cost, risks and schedule of starting both water projects earlier {{vote:m7}}.

debate: Industry delegates welcomed the new capacity but urged faster action to restore lender confidence. One delegate said the servicing agreement framework should not tie milestones to occupancy or bar lot sales before occupancy, and asked Council to delay approval.

Councillors asked how the framework would avoid perceived favouritism. Staff pointed to minimum agreement content, eligibility limited to requests made before May 6, 2026, and prioritizing by request date. One councillor said developers need certainty to get financing.

On the procurement waiver, staff said it would speed projects and that monthly reporting and the Chief Purchasing Officer's review would keep oversight. Councillors worried about sole sourcing, bias and transparency. They also questioned handing broad authority to staff just before a new Council term, which led to the shorter end date.

Delegates on groundwater asked for annual rather than biennial monitoring reports, trend analysis and proactive private well monitoring. They also asked for a more collaborative well interference process. Staff said feedback is being collected through consultation, including a July 14 session, and one councillor asked for a plain-language overview of the monitoring reports.

On the financial update, councillors said the forecast rate increases would be hard for residents and area municipalities to absorb. Staff stressed the scenarios are illustrative and that outside funding is the biggest factor in limiting rate pressure.
